The logical-path grammar identity-and-evidence section 3 already states: relative, slash-separated, no empty/dot/dot-dot/NUL/backslash segment, each segment at most 255 characters. THREE DIFFERENT ENFORCEMENTS EXIST AND THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT; this description states only where each applies and changes no accepted path set. (1) DIRECT $ref, exactly two fields: #/$defs/Blob/properties/path and #/$defs/import-blob/properties/path. Only these carry the full declarative grammar, INCLUDING the at-most-255-characters-per-segment bound. (2) fact/anchors[]/path: a plain bounded string here, additionally subject to the imperative recursive check in foundation/identity-model.py `ordered()` AND to a real snapshot JOIN - an anchor path must be an inventoried snapshot path, and inventory rows ARE Blob, so the declarative grammar reaches it through that join. (3) finding-fingerprint/subjectKey/logicalPath: a plain bounded string subject to the SAME imperative `ordered()` check and to NO snapshot join. `ordered()` refuses, for any string under a key named `path` or `logicalPath` at any depth, a leading slash, a backslash, a NUL and any empty/dot/dot-dot segment - and it does NOT enforce the per-segment 255 maximum. So (3) is not equivalently constrained to (1), and no snapshot join is claimed for it. The three scope-descriptor path arrays deliberately reference none of this, because `.` alone denotes the admitted project root and this grammar forbids a dot segment. Byte-identical in constraint to workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/LogicalPath, which is what makes the import blob rows an exact mirror.
Registered digest-domain name. This enumeration and #/$defs/Ref/properties/domain are the same set, and both are the registered keys of x-opensip-digest-domains.byDomain.

A retained blob row of an import. Identical to Blob except for the import unit's own published hostile-input artifact bound (imported-evidence.schema.json: 'artifact at most 268435456 bytes'), which is an import bound and deliberately not imposed on source-inventory or closure tree rows. Exact mirror of workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/Blob.

The closed inventory of the import's retained AUXILIARY ASSET members. It is not the import's mandatory custody: the payload bytes and the exact registered schema DOCUMENT bytes are retained and re-hashed independently by registered_payload, and those obligations hold identically when this array is empty. An archive member outside this list is never read (native-evidence section 3 PO-4) - a restriction on READING, satisfied vacuously by an empty list, never a requirement that a member exist. minItems 0 is therefore the owning admissibility: a self-contained normalized payload may legitimately retain no auxiliary asset. An earlier revision of this description required minItems 1, arguing that adapterClosure asserts an adapter ran over the bytes named by the custody record's sourcePath; that argument was withdrawn because ImportedEvidenceRecordV1.sourcePath is a UserInputPath, which the workflow common schema defines as never entering any content identity and recorded in operational records only, and because no join anywhere binds sourcePath to a member of this array. Requiring one arbitrary blob would not establish original-input custody. maxItems 4096 and the item byte bound are the import unit's own published hostile-input bounds (workflows/schemas/imported-evidence.schema.json top-level description: at most 4096 blobs, artifact at most 268435456 bytes); the foundation record previously allowed 100000, and narrowing to the published bound is a stated compatibility change.

Declared output-domain set. Empty is permitted and asserts no output domains; it does not establish completeness or result authority. Stage and stage-spec sets must agree.

This field enters PlanId through analysisSpecDigest and was previously $ref Text with no named vocabulary, so two conforming hosts requesting the same analysis of the same unit minted different PlanIds. The pattern here is the product-configuration analysis.capabilities item pattern - it contains no `@`, so a relation@rung spelling is refused by shape - and it is NECESSARY, never sufficient: membership in the closed matrix vocabulary and applicability of the (capability, languageMode) cell are decided at admission. A capability id is a requestable unit of work and is deliberately NOT a relation@rung fact/Coverage coordinate; the matrix publishes the bridge both ways.

Within ONE analysis-spec the ownership tuple is UNIQUE. Two rows carrying the same (capabilityId, languageMode, workspaceRoot) are refused whatever their `required` values are; there is deliberately no last-wins, no order dependence and no merge of requiredness, so a caller states one value per cell or the record is refused.

The tuple names one cell of work for one unit and `required` is that cell's attribute. Two disagreeing rows leave requiredness undetermined for a cell whose value decides an indeterminate contribution, and BOTH rows enter analysisSpecDigest and therefore PlanId - so the contradiction is committed, not transient. native section 1.4 already refuses a duplicate capabilityId in the RELEASE declaration for exactly this reason; this is the analysis-spec's own analogue, published here because this is the record's owning schema.
The deterministic analysis budget. identity-and-evidence section 3 requires plan.budget to equal this value exactly and by type; an override is made here first so both committed places agree.
The snapshot source inventory as a registered record in its own right, so that vcs-observation.sourceInventoryDigest names a record rather than an unnamed canonical fragment.

The closed record digested by predicate-witness.programPredicateDigest. It addresses ONE predicate node of the admitted RuleProgramV1; it introduces no second policy language. predicateId is the node address: the rule root is "p", the i-th operand of an and/or node at address a is a+"."+i (zero-based, shortest decimal), and the operand of a not node at address a is a+".0".
equal to the proof bundle ruleProgramDigest this witness belongs to
raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of the exact predicate node the rule program carries at rules[ruleId].emitWhen addressed by predicateId; its op equals operation

The closed record digested by finding.parameterDigest. parameters is an object map so that parameter names are unique and ordered by the canonical encoder itself, with no ordering annotation to elect.

The closed record digested by stageSpecDigest. execution-plan.stages[].stageSpecDigest and cache-key.stageSpecDigest are the SAME field name because they are the same digest of the same record under the same recipe; there are not two recipes for one spelling.

The closed record digested by commit-receipt.inventoryDigest: the exact set of typed object identities and retained raw blob digests the commit published for this Run.
The closed record digested by semantic-grant.principals[].ownerSourceDigest: the security contract RepoExecutionGrantV2 owner projection, strictly ascending and unique by ownerKey UTF-8 bytes.

The closed record whose raw SHA-256 is the languageVersion component of a FACT-IDENTITY body frame. Retention is DERIVED: no field of it is a free input, every field is copied from a named path in a record this Run already retains and the owning contract already admitted, and Run closure recomputes it rather than accepting it. Two conforming implementations build identical bytes from the same committed Run, which is what the inherited obligation "canonical identity bytes supplied by ResolvedInputs/PlanId, not a human display string" asks for. It is hashed, not embedded, because the inherited frame gives each component a u8 length and a component built by embedding per-crate data is not representable for valid inputs.

The language of the BODY, which is not always the language of the provider. Native section 6.3 puts languageId in the normalized-body preimage and closes it to {typescript, javascript, rust} so that a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript one even with identical bytes. One TypeScript engine universe produces bodies of BOTH: the engine is the provider, the source variant decides the body language, and section 6.4 keeps cross-TS/JS matching a separate candidate-only projection rather than a shared identity.
The component that INTERPRETS the body span. Not the build tool and not the resolver.

The release identity of that component, taken from the admitted native context. admit_native_context already refuses native.native-context-compiler-version-not-from-manifest unless it equals the admitted tool closure semanticVersion, for both languages, so this is joined to a retained closure manifest and is not a copied display string.

The exact build of that component: rustCommitHash for rust, compilerPackageDigest for typescript. Not a 64-hex field of this bundle and deliberately not annotated as one: it is an owner-admitted identity carried inside a derived record, joined by equality to the retained context and never re-hashed here. Its width differs by language by construction.

The dialect axis of a GRAMMAR-ONLY interpretation; used only by the syntax-only universe. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so it has no edition to select and no tsconfig program to join. Claiming an edition for a .rs body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics, and reusing sourceVariant would let a grammar-parsed body carry the identical dialect token as a compiler-parsed one. The token is the variant the bundled grammar selects from the body's own suffix. Because this is a DIFFERENT branch, a syntax-only body identity can never collide with a compiler-derived identity over the same bytes - which is the intended distinction, not a defect: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different interpretations of the span and equating them would be a false clone claim.

The SELECTED source-language dialect of the body being identified: the edition of its owning compilation unit, the source variant its own suffix denotes, or - for a grammar-only interpretation - the grammar variant that suffix selects. Never a whole map and never null - a language with no declared dialect axis would be an unexamined default, and there is none. Including a map would make one body identity depend on unrelated crates and would not be representable inside the inherited u8 component length.

Normative machine-readable registry for identity-and-evidence section 3. Every 64-hex field in this bundle carries x-opensip-digest; a field without one is not admissible. domainSets additionally name the owning contract admission that Run closure must re-run over the retained frame, the retained closure joins it must re-derive, and the snapshot joins its paths must satisfy.

The native context of the syntax-only mode. It carries exactly what interprets a body span when there is no compiler: the retained, closure-bound GRAMMAR BUNDLE and the normalizer specification it uses. It deliberately has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no node_modules layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis reads none of them; a syntax-only context that named a compiler would be claiming semantics it never computed.

The universe of the syntax-only mode. `semantic universe` names the thing that DETERMINES a fact, and for a grammar-only analysis that is the selected bundled-grammar set, not a compiler semantic model. It exists because the capability matrix advertises declares/literal/control-flow at `syntactic` and clones at `normalized-body-hash` for syntax-only, and because file/package/vcs-change inventory facts must be representable in a repository that contains no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all: fact2 and subject-scope both REQUIRE a universe h-identity from this closed domain set, so with only the two compiler universes registered those advertised cells could mint no fact and no scope. Making the universe fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact states what produced it, and would leave `which grammar read this body` unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on it. Semantic capability is NOT widened by this domain - a syntax-only universe can carry only the syntactic and inventory rungs and the clones rung; imports/references/calls/types/reachability remain language-tier-unsupported, and a universal negative still requires its own complete Coverage.

native-evidence LanguageMode -> the native universe language it requests. syntax-only requests the `syntax` universe: it requests no COMPILER universe, which is a different statement from requesting none at all. It previously mapped to null, and because fact2/subject-scope require a universe h-identity from a closed set of two compiler domains, the syntax and clones cells the capability matrix advertises for that mode - and every file/package/vcs-change fact in a repository with no TypeScript or Rust unit - could mint no fact and no scope.
Which closure kind each closure-bearing field admits. Stated so no field is left to guess.

No new closure kind is invented for producer acts: enumeration, view production, fact production and stage production are all provider acts under the existing kind. `grammar` is a genuinely new INSTALLED-COMPONENT kind, in the same family as `toolchain`, `stdlib` and `rust-dev-llvm`: the syntax-only mode's body interpreter is a bundled grammar set, and binding it to an existing kind would either claim it is a toolchain (it executes no compiler) or leave the component that interprets a body span outside the closure law, which is the one thing every other universe pins down.

Normative, and consumed by BOTH the native producer admission boundary and identity Run closure. It states what a COVERAGE claim over a body-dialect relation means under a universe whose dialect form is a closed suffix table. The per-BODY selector (`dialect.onUnknown`) was already total, but it is only reached while a body is being derived, so a scope that produced NO fact was classified by nothing and could claim a determinate `complete` for a path the universe cannot read in any dialect. Coverage is a claim about the EXAMINATION and must not be decided by whether the examination happened to produce output.
Plan selection bindings for authoritative inputs; companion to closureKinds. Unreferenced CAS blobs are not evaluation inputs.

Normative closed registry for every registered PAYLOAD in this graph. It resolves the question a payload schema digest alone cannot: which document bytes are hashed and which selector validates. It is the single mapping identity-and-evidence section 3 names; nothing in this graph admits a payload under a caller-chosen or guessed schema.

The 13 rows live in the document itself so relation, selector, universe rule and rung ladder cannot drift from the schemas they describe. fact.resolution must be a rung of the row ladder, the rung required/forbidden field rules apply, and universeRule same-only requires fact.sourceUniverse == fact.targetUniverse.
The Run closure re-derives these rows from the workflow registry and refuses if they differ, so one registry cannot drift from the other.

The workflow glob scope-policy document that comparison-result EvaluationContext.scopeDigest names and that the comparison contract requires to be bound as an analysis-spec parameter. With the class closed to one document that binding refused at Plan admission, so the comparison scope axis could not be populated at all. This row is deliberately a DIFFERENT record from the foundation scope-descriptor that plan.scopeDigest names: scope-descriptor is the repository extent actually walked (workspace roots and path prefixes), ScopeDocumentV1 is the policy's include/exclude glob selection over that extent. Both may appear in one Plan; neither substitutes for the other.

An analysis-spec or stage-spec parameter may only cite a document on this closed list. That replaces the withdrawn "a payload schema document must constrain the payload directly" rule, which contradicted the native and workflow bundle registries. A cited schema with no row refuses: there is no default row, no caller-selected schema and no permissive fallback for an unregistered parameter.

ONE Plan selects AT MOST ONE parameter per registered row. Zero is legal for a row this analysis does not need; two or more entries of analysis-spec.parameters (or stage-spec.parameters) whose schemaDigest resolves to the SAME row are REFUSED, whatever their payloadDigests are. This is a SELECTION rule about how many entries a SPEC may carry and is a different question from keyIsTheDocumentNotThePair, which is about how many REGISTRY ROWS one document digest may resolve to; PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW answers the second and never constrained the first.

A parameter row is a Plan INPUT: the payload it cites is the value the analysis is run with. Two entries under one row put two different values in one input slot and nothing decides which is the Plan's. Both enter analysisSpecDigest and therefore PlanId, so two conforming hosts could bind different documents from ONE admitted Plan and the resulting comparison axis would attribute differently for the same PlanId. Refusing is the registry declining an arbitrary selection, exactly as it does for an ambiguous row. There is deliberately NO default, NO first-listed or last-listed winner, and NO merge.

It is not the import's mandatory custody: the payload bytes and the exact registered schema DOCUMENT bytes are retained and re-hashed independently by registered_payload, and those obligations hold identically when this array is empty. An archive member outside this list is never read (native-evidence section 3 PO-4) - a restriction on READING, satisfied vacuously by an empty list, never a requirement that a member exist. minItems 0 is therefore the owning admissibility: a self-contained normalized payload may legitimately retain no auxiliary asset. An earlier revision of this description required minItems 1, arguing that adapterClosure asserts an adapter ran over the bytes named by the custody record's sourcePath; that argument was withdrawn because ImportedEvidenceRecordV1.sourcePath is a UserInputPath, which the workflow common schema defines as never entering any content identity and recorded in operational records only, and because no join anywhere binds sourcePath to a member of this array. Requiring one arbitrary blob would not establish original-input custody. maxItems 4096 and the item byte bound are the import unit's own published hostile-input bounds (workflows/schemas/imported-evidence.schema.json top-level description: at most 4096 blobs, artifact at most 268435456 bytes); the foundation record previously allowed 100000, and narrowing to the published bound is a stated compatibility change.

The closed record whose raw SHA-256 is the languageVersion component of a FACT-IDENTITY body frame. Retention is DERIVED: no field of it is a free input, every field is copied from a named path in a record this Run already retains and the owning contract already admitted, and Run closure recomputes it rather than accepting it. Two conforming implementations build identical bytes from the same committed Run, which is what the inherited obligation "canonical identity bytes supplied by ResolvedInputs/PlanId, not a human display string" asks for. It is hashed, not embedded, because the inherited frame gives each component a u8 length and a component built by embedding per-crate data is not representable for valid inputs.

The language of the BODY, which is not always the language of the provider. Native section 6.3 puts languageId in the normalized-body preimage and closes it to {typescript, javascript, rust} so that a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript one even with identical bytes. One TypeScript engine universe produces bodies of BOTH: the engine is the provider, the source variant decides the body language, and section 6.4 keeps cross-TS/JS matching a separate candidate-only projection rather than a shared identity.
The component that INTERPRETS the body span. Not the build tool and not the resolver.

The release identity of that component, taken from the admitted native context. admit_native_context already refuses native.native-context-compiler-version-not-from-manifest unless it equals the admitted tool closure semanticVersion, for both languages, so this is joined to a retained closure manifest and is not a copied display string.

The exact build of that component: rustCommitHash for rust, compilerPackageDigest for typescript. Not a 64-hex field of this bundle and deliberately not annotated as one: it is an owner-admitted identity carried inside a derived record, joined by equality to the retained context and never re-hashed here. Its width differs by language by construction.

The dialect axis of a GRAMMAR-ONLY interpretation; used only by the syntax-only universe. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so it has no edition to select and no tsconfig program to join. Claiming an edition for a .rs body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics, and reusing sourceVariant would let a grammar-parsed body carry the identical dialect token as a compiler-parsed one. The token is the variant the bundled grammar selects from the body's own suffix. Because this is a DIFFERENT branch, a syntax-only body identity can never collide with a compiler-derived identity over the same bytes - which is the intended distinction, not a defect: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different interpretations of the span and equating them would be a false clone claim.

The SELECTED source-language dialect of the body being identified: the edition of its owning compilation unit, the source variant its own suffix denotes, or - for a grammar-only interpretation - the grammar variant that suffix selects. Never a whole map and never null - a language with no declared dialect axis would be an unexamined default, and there is none. Including a map would make one body identity depend on unrelated crates and would not be representable inside the inherited u8 component length.

Configuration-qualified subject. File/symbol native IDs are unique in kind/universe. Package names can repeat at different first-party manifests, so packageManifestPath is a required package-only coordinate. No synthetic native package spelling or encounter-order suffix.

Exact row address within the payload selected by importId. execution selects the TestPayload as a whole; other selectors select subjects[ordinal] or tests[ordinal]. Owner admission checks kind/selector, bounds and explicit Plan/evaluation-input membership. This new descriptor is inline in its witness and is not assigned fragment retention.

The typed cause carried beside a DeficiencyV2 in a Coverage entry. The three body-language-* members are the clones ownership states that identity-and-evidence and native-evidence section 11 require the clones Coverage to DISCLOSE: the contract mandates that such a scope mint no body identity, that its Coverage report the incompleteness, and that the predicate and seal be indeterminate rather than a false pass -- and until these members existed no value in this closed vocabulary could name why. A nullable nativeCause does not satisfy a mandated disclosure; a null there records that a disclosure was owed and not made. The other selectionLaw causes deliberately have NO member here: BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_COMPILED and BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_SELECTED are per-body refusals that section 11 states are compatible with coverage=complete (the host examined that subject and correctly produced no fact for it), and BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_ABSENT/BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_AMBIGUOUS are universe-level dialect faults that refuse before any Coverage entry is minted.

Normative machine-readable registry for identity-and-evidence section 3. Every 64-hex field in this bundle carries x-opensip-digest; a field without one is not admissible. domainSets additionally name the owning contract admission that Run closure must re-run over the retained frame, the retained closure joins it must re-derive, and the snapshot joins its paths must satisfy.

The native context of the syntax-only mode. It carries exactly what interprets a body span when there is no compiler: the retained, closure-bound GRAMMAR BUNDLE and the normalizer specification it uses. It deliberately has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no node_modules layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis reads none of them; a syntax-only context that named a compiler would be claiming semantics it never computed.

The universe of the syntax-only mode. `semantic universe` names the thing that DETERMINES a fact, and for a grammar-only analysis that is the selected bundled-grammar set, not a compiler semantic model. It exists because the capability matrix advertises declares/literal/control-flow at `syntactic` and clones at `normalized-body-hash` for syntax-only, and because file/package/vcs-change inventory facts must be representable in a repository that contains no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all: fact2 and subject-scope both REQUIRE a universe h-identity from this closed domain set, so with only the two compiler universes registered those advertised cells could mint no fact and no scope. Making the universe fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact states what produced it, and would leave `which grammar read this body` unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on it. Semantic capability is NOT widened by this domain - a syntax-only universe can carry only the syntactic and inventory rungs and the clones rung; imports/references/calls/types/reachability remain language-tier-unsupported, and a universal negative still requires its own complete Coverage.

native-evidence LanguageMode -> the native universe language it requests. syntax-only requests the `syntax` universe: it requests no COMPILER universe, which is a different statement from requesting none at all. It previously mapped to null, and because fact2/subject-scope require a universe h-identity from a closed set of two compiler domains, the syntax and clones cells the capability matrix advertises for that mode - and every file/package/vcs-change fact in a repository with no TypeScript or Rust unit - could mint no fact and no scope.
Which closure kind each closure-bearing field admits. Stated so no field is left to guess.

No new closure kind is invented for producer acts: enumeration, view production, fact production and stage production are all provider acts under the existing kind. `grammar` is a genuinely new INSTALLED-COMPONENT kind, in the same family as `toolchain`, `stdlib` and `rust-dev-llvm`: the syntax-only mode's body interpreter is a bundled grammar set, and binding it to an existing kind would either claim it is a toolchain (it executes no compiler) or leave the component that interprets a body span outside the closure law, which is the one thing every other universe pins down.

Normative, and consumed by BOTH the native producer admission boundary and identity Run closure. It states what a COVERAGE claim over a body-dialect relation means under a universe whose dialect form is a closed suffix table. The per-BODY selector (`dialect.onUnknown`) was already total, but it is only reached while a body is being derived, so a scope that produced NO fact was classified by nothing and could claim a determinate `complete` for a path the universe cannot read in any dialect. Coverage is a claim about the EXAMINATION and must not be decided by whether the examination happened to produce output.
Plan selection bindings for authoritative inputs; companion to closureKinds. Unreferenced CAS blobs are not evaluation inputs.

Normative closed registry for every registered PAYLOAD in this graph. It resolves the question a payload schema digest alone cannot: which document bytes are hashed and which selector validates. The 13 rows live in the document itself so relation, selector, universe rule and rung ladder cannot drift from the schemas they describe. fact.resolution must be a rung of the row ladder, the rung required/forbidden field rules apply, and universeRule same-only requires fact.sourceUniverse == fact.targetUniverse.

ONE Plan selects AT MOST ONE parameter per registered row. Zero is legal for a row this analysis does not need; two or more entries of analysis-spec.parameters (or stage-spec.parameters) whose schemaDigest resolves to the SAME row are REFUSED, whatever their payloadDigests are. This is a SELECTION rule about how many entries a SPEC may carry and is a different question from keyIsTheDocumentNotThePair, which is about how many REGISTRY ROWS one document digest may resolve to; PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW answers the second and never constrained the first.

A parameter row is a Plan INPUT: the payload it cites is the value the analysis is run with. Two entries under one row put two different values in one input slot and nothing decides which is the Plan's. Both enter analysisSpecDigest and therefore PlanId, so two conforming hosts could bind different documents from ONE admitted Plan and the resulting comparison axis would attribute differently for the same PlanId. Refusing is the registry declining an arbitrary selection, exactly as it does for an ambiguous row. There is deliberately NO default, NO first-listed or last-listed winner, and NO merge.

Normative and CLOSED. Every relation row carries an `anchorLaw`; there is no default and no unstated relation. It decides how many `fact.anchors` entries a fact of that relation carries, and therefore whether one semantic input has one spelling or several.

A code fact is READ FROM SOURCE TEXT, so it must name at least one anchor: the span it was read from. An unanchored code fact names no file that could have been read and is refused (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`). This was previously enforced only inside the syntax-universe capability guard, so the same unanchored `declares` or `references` fact closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe; the law is one law and now binds in every universe.

Unchanged from the existing `bodyIdentityJoin.anchorCardinality`: exactly the body span the identity is over. Zero would leave the claim unattached and several would make the L0 recomputation a choice.

An inventory fact is NOT read from a source span. Its whole semantic input is its payload, and that payload is already bound to the snapshot by this relation's own `snapshotJoins`: the path must be in the snapshot inventory, and for `file` the content digest, the byte length and CUSTODY of the exact retained bytes are joined as well. An anchor could only restate a subset of a claim that is already joined, and because nothing derives it, it is a free axis that gives one semantic input several spellings and several identities. It is therefore closed at zero (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).

Normative and CLOSED. A relation row carries a `coverageTotality` row only where the relation's own meaning makes its rung TOTAL over the snapshot inventory. A relation with no row declares that a subject may lawfully bear no fact, which is itself the record that nothing further constrains it.

`entry.coverage: complete` is a claim that the committed examined partition was examined exhaustively. For a rung that is total over the inventory that claim also decides a universal negative: over a COMPLETE `file@enumerated` Coverage, `exists file where path=P` is authoritative, so a complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject asserts that an inventoried file is ABSENT. On frozen v13 that graph closed - a `file@enumerated` scope over the inventoried subject `a.ts`, `coverage: complete`, `deficiency: null` and zero facts. Nothing derived the obligation, so nothing refused it.

Normative and CLOSED. The DISJOINTNESS half of identity-and-evidence section 3's `Coverage scopes partition the claimed universe without overlaps or omissions`. The OMISSION half is coverageTotalityLaw above and is owed only where a relation carries a coverageTotality row. These two halves have different owners and different decidability, and neither implies the other.

The clause was stated and nothing derived or compared it. A retained Run could carry two subject-scopes of ONE view with the same snapshot, relation, rung and both universes whose subject sets intersect, and close. What that demonstrates is that an INVALID partition was ACCEPTED: the same subject was committed twice under one interpretation, so a claim read over that view - a count, a completeness claim or a universal negative - can be ambiguous or double-counted depending on how a consumer joins the scopes. It is NOT asserted that every consumer necessarily double-counts; what is established, and what this law fixes, is that the published partition property was not decided anywhere. That is the same defect class as the frozen-reference file@enumerated omission.

Which member is legal on a given entry is decided by RC-1 (native-evidence.md section 4.3) and is NOT schema-decidable: applicability is total over the registered (relation, rung) pairs and turns on membership of the RUNG in the closed five-member resolved set (resolved-target, resolved-binding, resolved-callee, checked, from-resolved-calls), never on the relation ladder length. A resolved rung must never be not-applicable - reachability@from-resolved-calls is a one-rung relation whose single rung IS resolved - and every other registered rung, including unresolved-edge@observed and types@annotated as well as the syntactic rungs, is not-applicable with attempted=false, unresolvedEdgeCount=0 and unresolvedEdgeClasses=[]. RC-0 runs first and is relation-specific: the pair must be registered, meaning the rung is a member of THAT relation's own ladder, so unresolved-edge@enumerated is refused although both tokens are registered. That check and the not-applicable minting law (attempted false, count 0, empty class list) are enforced by coverage_bijection at the producer boundary AND again at retained Run closure, and they hold for a FACT-FREE entry over an empty examined scope. not-applicable is never a fallback for an unregistered pair. stageTerminal is deliberately not constrained: a not-applicable entry may retain the stage terminal its producer observed.
