The ANSWER over the examined partition, and the second committed encoding of the section 4.1 claim-1 question `did we look at every subject?`. RC-6, enforced by the cross-property admission check rather than encoded in this shape schema: coverage=complete REQUIRES resolutionCompleteness.examinedExhaustive=true. It is an IMPLICATION, never an equality. coverage=unknown constrains examinedExhaustive in NEITHER direction: a host may examine the committed partition exhaustively and still answer unknown because the evidence it needs is missing rather than unexamined (ambiguous or missing Rust compilation ownership, an undeclared or unservable capability, an unlisted source variant), and it may also answer unknown because the examination itself was cut short. Only the converse is impossible: complete over a partition the producer says it did not examine exhaustively asserts a totality the same record disclaims. RC-6 says nothing about resolutionCompleteness.state - enumeration completeness and RESOLUTION completeness are different claims, and RC-3's coverage=complete with state=incomplete over real unresolved edges stays lawful. It is total over every registered (relation, rung) pair including the twelve non-resolved ones, holds for a fact-free entry over an empty examined scope, and is enforced by coverage_bijection at the producer boundary (admit_coverage_result_v3) AND again at retained Run closure, whose disagreement is PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION on the existing native.coverage-bijection-mismatch carrier - no new key and no new public detail.
the 64-hex suffix of the closure2 identity of the admitted kind=rust-dev-llvm closure

Raw SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the SINGLE projected .cargo/config.toml file the adapter materializes under CC-5. It is a raw artifact digest of a file, not an H identity, and it is NOT rust-v2.configProjectionSha256, which is the 64-hex suffix of H(native.cargo-config-projection.v2, CargoConfigProjectionV2) over this whole record (section 3.3).

The verified-carrier Cargo configuration projection. Its own H domain is native.cargo-config-projection.v2; rust-v2.configProjectionSha256 carries the 64-hex suffix of that identity, and projectionSha256 inside this record is the raw digest of the projected config FILE.

The installed, closure-bound grammar bundle that a syntax-only analysis parses with. It is the component that INTERPRETS a body span in that mode, so it is pinned exactly the way a toolchain is: closureId names an admitted kind=grammar closure, parserVersion must equal that closure manifest's semanticVersion (admission refuses native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest otherwise, mirroring the compiler-version rule), and bundleDigest is the exact retained bundle identity. `grammars` is the CLOSED bundled-grammar set: it is what native-evidence section 1.2's 'any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar' actually denotes, and what makes `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` decidable rather than a matter of taste.
The component that reads the body span. Not a compiler: a syntax-only universe executes none, and naming one here would claim an interpretation that never happened.

Every language the host actually bundles a grammar for, matching BUNDLED_GRAMMARS exactly. An earlier revision listed only typescript/javascript/rust and claimed equality with the body-language-version enum as a drift check; that could not express the four data/document grammars the host has always bundled, so native-evidence section 1.2's 'any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar' was unrepresentable for them. What is actually held equal to the body-language-version enum is the set of languages whose grammars are syntaxClass=code - see syntaxClass.

Which capability this grammar's files bear, and the exact distinction the original contracts already draw. `code`: the language has the body spans native-evidence section 6.3 defines - function, method, closure/lambda, impl item and block bodies - and a published L1-L3 normalisation table, so its files can bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations. Its languageId MUST be a member of the foundation body-language-version languageId enum, because that identifier goes into the clone preimage. `data-document`: a bundled grammar for a data or document format with no such body spans and no published tokenisation, literalKind mapping or normalisation law anywhere in this kit. Its files are grammar-only members - accounted, never `unsupported-file` - and bear inventory evidence (file/package/vcs-change); they mint no body identity, and its languageId MUST NOT be in the body-language-version enum, since it can never appear in a clone preimage. Claiming code-construct syntax facts for a data format would require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, which is exactly the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to avoid.

The clone normalisation component this bundle ships. It is recorded so the clones rung has a bound owner in syntax-only mode; it is deliberately NOT part of the body-language-version record, because the normalisation level specification is already its own framed component of the body identity.

The native context of the syntax-only language mode. It carries exactly the grammar bundle that interprets a body span and nothing else: no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no node_modules layout, no config graph. Those all belong to resolution, and a grammar-only analysis performs none. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would be asserting semantics the mode never computes.

The universe of the syntax-only mode. Its identity is the admitted grammar context plus the SELECTED grammar set for this analysis: selecting a different grammar set is a different universe, exactly as selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is visible to every consumer rather than being an invisible default. It carries the constant resolutionAttempted=false so no consumer can read a syntax-only universe as a resolution claim: semantic rungs under it are language-tier-unsupported, not merely absent.

A subset of the context bundle's grammarIds. Admission refuses a selection naming a grammar the bundle does not contain; an empty selection is not expressible, because a universe that parsed nothing could not have produced a fact.

The 64-hex suffix of H(native.cargo-config-projection.v2, CargoConfigProjectionV2) over the bound context configProjection record. A bare DigestHex, never a Sha256Text, and never the raw SHA-256 of the canonical projection bytes.

Required and nullable, exactly as preparedOutputSetId is. null means NO committed ownership: such a universe admits no clones fact AT ALL, whatever its edition map looks like. An earlier revision of this description said null was admissible 'only while the edition map has a single distinct value, where every body has the same dialect and no owner selection arises'. That was the withdrawn package-default fast path and it is contradicted by the retained selectionLaw and by body_language_version, which refuses on missing ownership unconditionally: Cargo lets a target override its package default, so even a single-valued edition map can contain targets at different effective editions, and agreeing package defaults therefore never determine a body's dialect. The nullable form is retained deliberately - a universe whose ownership is unavailable or only partially enumerated is a legitimate retained universe; it simply mints no body identity, its clones Coverage carries the typed ownership disclosure (deficiency input-closure-incomplete with the matching body-language-* nativeCause), and its empty clone view stays indeterminate rather than becoming a finding of no clones.

executionCapableResolution=true means only that prepared products of some execution were consumed as inert data (preparedResolution != none). It is never a host execution grant; the grant is the operational RepoExecutionGrantV1 reference outside Plan.
Blob reference. mediaType is a declared label and never a trust proof: admissibility is decided by row kind and consumption channel (PO-0).
Operational H(security.repo-execution-grants.v2,{schemaVersion:2,grantRefs:sorted unique v2 grant references}); one admitted grant per preparation owner. Not a semantic Plan field.
SUPERSEDED DRAFT transport shape; no product admission path. Workflow ReviewDisposition is the sole current candidate suppression record.
Typed detail beside an EXISTING D9 code: the deficiency and nativeCause live in the coverage2 record named by the termination's coverageId. No successor codes.

The published vocabulary authority for analysis-spec requestedCapabilities[].capabilityId, product-configuration analysis.capabilities and the authenticated release declaration registry. `members` is held equal to capabilities[].id by the reference checks, so the law cannot drift from the table it governs.
files at or below an admitted boundary (P3): another project's or uncustodied source, disclosed, never scanned and never erased
INPUT ADAPTER SHAPE ONLY (was RuntimeCoveragePayloadV1). Never an admitted import payload: the native adapter normalizes it to the single canonical workflow payload before import2 (contract §7).
INPUT ADAPTER SHAPE ONLY (was TestResultsPayloadV1). Never an admitted import payload: the native adapter normalizes it to the single canonical workflow payload before import2 (contract §7).
INPUT ADAPTER SHAPE ONLY (was HistoryPayloadV1). Never an admitted import payload: the native adapter normalizes it to the single canonical workflow payload before import2 (contract §7).

a security excludedUnits row (relative form) whose reason is a custody/depth exclusion; DIRECTORY_CUSTODY/DEPTH exclude the directory and everything below it, MARKER_CUSTODY excludes exactly that marker file

TRUSTED ADMITTED INPUT (P3): the security discovery instrument's authority boundaries for the selected root, converted once by discovery-defaults.boundary_inventory_from_provenance from the ACCEPTed DiscoveryProvenanceV1 (absolute custody locators -> relative scope paths). Never authored by a caller; an operational host composition passes it to discover_units/assign_membership/unit_scope_descriptor.
boundary provenance of a unit discovery: source `security.discovery` when the admitted inventory was applied, `none` for the standalone pure instrument (not an operational host composition)
The effective moduleResolution the admitted compiler applies. It changes which specifiers resolve, so it is a native-context field and a universe key.

Declaration-file BASENAME of a `.d.ts` member of the admitted stdlib closure tree, e.g. lib.es2022.d.ts - not a lib name and not a tree path. The row set is the COMPLETE inventory of those members, selected or not, so the selection never narrows it; a tree with two paths sharing a basename refuses native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename> because the libSelection join published in native-evidence.md section 2.4, component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts" with fold the full non-tailored default lowercase mapping, would not have a unique target.
the semanticVersion of the ADMITTED signed compiler closure manifest; never the output of an unverified `tsc --version`

identity-and-evidence section 3: the 64-hex SUFFIX of the closure2 identity of the admitted kind=stdlib closure, exactly as ToolchainIdentityV1.rustcDevLlvmDigest is the suffix of the kind=rust-dev-llvm closure. A bare DigestHex, never a Sha256Text: the typed prefix belongs to the foundation closure2 identity it was taken from, and `closure2:` + this value must name a retained closure whose recomputed identity equals it.
the 64-hex suffix of the closure2 identity of the admitted kind=stdlib closure

The COMPLETE declaration-file inventory of the admitted stdlib closure tree, selected or not: one row per `.d.ts` member, `component` = the member basename, `sha256` = its raw digest, sorted by component UTF-8 bytes. Admission refuses a missing row (an alternate partial inventory for the same retained library is not the required complete record) and refuses a tree in which two paths share a basename, because the join would be ambiguous.

The effective `lib` NAMES the resolved compilerOptions select (after target defaulting), sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the retained unfolded names. These are lib names (es2022, dom), NOT declaration-file names. native-evidence.md section 2.4 publishes the join to standardLibraryComponentDigests: with fold(n) the Unicode Default Case Conversion toLowercase(X) - the FULL, non-tailored, context-sensitive default lowercase mapping, NOT Simple_Lowercase_Mapping and NOT Case_Folding, bound to native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION and implemented by lib_name_fold; the same single fold the honoredOptions.lib agreement uses - component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts", and every component(n) must be an element of the declared component set, else native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>. The mapping is one-directional: a component is never mapped back into a selected name, and this array is never re-spelled into file names. The folded name set must also equal the folded honoredOptions.lib set; a duplicate under fold refuses native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection.

Every executable the TypeScript adapter may select: the bundled compiler and the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure2 named by closureId. No PATH lookup, no system `node`, no NODE_OPTIONS/NODE_PATH/TS_NODE_* from the environment.

The closed subset of the resolved compilerOptions that changes program membership, module resolution or checking. Every value is the EFFECTIVE post-resolution value of the admitted tsconfig graph (or of SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1 under js-synthesized), never a raw file field.
every tsconfig/jsconfig file in the resolved extends graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under configOrigin=synthesized
The TypeScript counterpart of CargoConfigProjectionV2. Stripping an option is disclosed here; it is never a reason to read the option from anywhere else.

Closed native context for the typescript-v2 universe; H domain `native.context.typescript.v2`. It carries no platform FIELD because TypeScript resolution semantics are platform-invariant by design (section 1.1); the identity is NOT platform-invariant, because toolClosure.closureId names a signed closure whose foundation descriptor includes `platform`, so two platform families running different executables mint two nativeContextIds. It is NOT NativeContextV2, which is the Rust context (targetTriple/hostTriple/cargo resolver); a typescript-v2 universe whose nativeContextId was minted from a Rust descriptor is refused.

which closed native-context record and H domain a universe binds. `syntax` is the grammar-only context of the syntax-only language mode: it names a bundled grammar set rather than a compiler, and a universe bound to it carries only the inventory, syntactic and clones rungs. It is a native-context selector, not a source language; the LANGUAGE of a body under it is still one of the closed body-language-version languageId values.

Host result of admitting one native context. nativeContextId is the Sha256Text the universe carries; planNativeContextDigest is the same 64 hex without the prefix, the spelling foundation plan.nativeContextDigests requires.

The producing result for the retained c2-plan-stage-schema.v4 coverage key field. subjectScopeCommitment is the SAME 64 hex as the foundation subject-scope identity scopeId, re-spelled in the native Sha256Text text form; it introduces no second preimage and no native H domain.

Result of the admitted native producer boundary for one CoverageResultV3 payload: the host mints scope2 from its own subject enumeration and refuses a payload whose committed key disagrees. A provider-supplied commitment is never authority.

The retained resolution read-set layout a TypeScript context commits to when nodeModulesInReadSet is true. One row per installed package DIRECTORY the resolver may read: installPath is the project-relative directory as the resolver walks it, realPath is the project-relative directory after symlink/workspace-link resolution (equal to installPath when there is no link), and contentSha256 is the raw SHA-256 of that package directory manifest file bytes (its package.json) as RETAINED, joined by digest. These rows are deliberately NOT snapshot inventory rows and must not be read as any: the one shared discovery rule prunes node_modules by path segment, so an inventory row could not exist for them, and the layout is a retained resolution observation of bytes the analysis actually read (native-evidence section 2.2, and the blobJoin -- not a snapshotJoin -- on the native.context.typescript.v2 nested record). The earlier wording said 'as inventoried in the snapshot', which contradicted both and would have led an implementer to add node_modules paths to the snapshot inventory. Rows are strictly ascending and unique by installPath, so one layout has one spelling. nodeModulesLayoutDigest is the raw SHA-256 of C(this record); it is null exactly when nodeModulesInReadSet is false.

Which recognized configuration file this node is. DERIVED from node.path by the closed table at #/x-opensip-config-node-kind-law, never asserted: exact case-sensitive basename `tsconfig.json` -> tsconfig, `jsconfig.json` -> jsconfig, every other basename -> other. The rule is total and applies to EVERY node, entry and non-entry alike. `other` is an ordinary value, not a defect: `tsconfig.build.json` reached as a base is `other`, and an explicitly selected custom-named configuration is an `other` ENTRY that still derives configOrigin tsconfig. This field is inside the hashed record, so the rule is an identity rule.
native/native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-config-node-kind-law/rule

The ORDERED resolved extends edges of this node, in the order the config declares them. TypeScript 5.0 supports multiple entries in `extends` and a LATER entry wins, so precedence is the array order and must be retained: an unordered set or a single edge cannot represent an ordinary modern configuration. Empty means this node extends nothing. Repeated edges are retained; this is a sequence, not a set.

The resolved tsconfig/jsconfig extends graph a TypeScript universe commits to. entryConfigPath is the SELECTED root config the program was opened with, null exactly when the configuration was synthesized; nodes is every config file actually read, strictly ascending and unique by path, each carrying its inventoried snapshot digest, its kind and its ORDERED resolved extends edges with later-wins precedence. configOrigin is derived from the ENTRY node kind, never from the whole set: a jsconfig.json that extends a shared base.json is a jsconfig program. Every node must be reachable from the entry, every edge must name another node, and the edge graph must be acyclic. tsconfigGraphHash is the raw SHA-256 of C(this record). A selected entry whose kind is other represents an explicitly selected custom-named TypeScript configuration and derives configOrigin tsconfig. Every node's `kind` is derived from its path by the closed exact-basename table at #/x-opensip-config-node-kind-law - entry and non-entry alike - and a node whose declared kind is not the derived one refuses.

The committed relation from a SNAPSHOT SOURCE PATH to the compilation TARGET that reads it, the closed table of those targets, and the EXPLICIT SELECTION of which of them this universe analyses. It exists because a body span dialect is a property of the compilation target: neither a crate-name-to-root map nor the package edition map can supply it, since #[path], files shared by several targets and several compilation contexts of one crate defeat a directory inference, and Cargo lets a target override its package default edition. Because this record is committed by H identity inside RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.sourceUnitOwnershipId, a different SELECTION is a different record, a different identity and therefore a DIFFERENT sourceUniverse: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is validly analysed under each, one selection at a time, with no change to any relation payload. Every row is a retained native observation; nothing here executes Cargo, a build script or a repository read, and nothing here qualifies a compiler or an enumerator.

complete: every compiled source path OF THE SELECTED UNITS has a row, so a path with no row is not compiled by any selected target. partial: the producer did not finish, so an owner INSIDE the selected scope may exist that is not listed. These are different claims and the second is not a weaker form of the first: an unlisted owner could contradict a listed one, so no clone body dialect is admissible under partial. That is checked BEFORE any row lookup, so partial discovery can never act as an implicit edition selection by hiding a conflicting owner. Partial evidence remains useful under the existing facts and Coverage law: the clones scope reports its incompleteness and the predicate is indeterminate, rather than a body identity being minted on an unbounded claim.

The closed table of compilation targets. Strictly unique by unitId, and unitId is a FUNCTION of the metadata, so two contradictory rows for one purported unit are a refusal rather than two units that differ by accident. A selection or an ownership row naming a unitId with no row here is an unbound caller label and is inadmissible.

H(native.compilation-unit.v1, UnitIdentityV1{schemaVersion:1, markerPath, targetKind, targetName}) over the very fields this row carries. DERIVED retention: nothing separate is retained because the preimage IS the row, and admission re-derives and compares (sourceUnitOwnership.unitId). Not an opaque digest - preimage record, domain and selector are all published - and not a delimiter label, which could stay injective only by narrowing admitted repository paths.

The inventoried manifest that declares this target: the same markerPath vocabulary WorkspaceUnitV2 already uses, cited rather than duplicated. WorkspaceUnitV2 and UnitMembershipV1 identify WORKSPACE units - cargo-package and cargo-workspace - which is the wrong granularity here, because one package holds several targets that may carry different editions; naming the marker joins the two rather than competing with them.
A key of the universe edition map, which supplies the package default.

The target's OWN edition when it sets one, null when it takes the package default. Cargo documents edition on a target as well as on a package: cargo-metadata lists targets[].edition and states the package edition is a DEFAULT individual targets may differ from. null DEFERS to the universe edition map for crateName, so the two committed places can never contradict: an override is explicit and visible, and its absence is explicit too.

The EXPLICIT analysis scope: the compilation targets this universe analyses. Every member must be a unitId of the units table. This is what makes a shared path representable at two editions without an ambiguous claim - two selections are two universes - and it is what distinguishes SELECTED SCOPE from INCOMPLETE ENUMERATION. An owner outside the selection is deliberately out of scope and its edition does not bear on a body; an unlisted owner INSIDE the selection is a gap in knowledge and refuses. Silently omitting a conflicting owner from the units table is not a selection: the omission is invisible, whereas a selection is committed in the identity.
The pure relation. It carries no edition and no metadata, so it cannot contradict the units table.

The closed PREIMAGE of a compilation unit identity, published here with its domain, codec and selector precisely so that unitId is not an opaque digest: any consumer can rebuild these four fields from the unit row that carries them and recompute the identity. A delimiter-joined label was the earlier draft and is WITHDRAWN - it was injective only by excluding # from markerPath, and a # in a repository directory is admissible under the canonical repository-path contract, so that recipe narrowed admitted paths to make a delimiter work. H over this projection needs no such restriction and is fixed width for every admitted path and name length.

The closing digest law of identity-and-evidence section 3, extended to this bundle. Every 64-hex or sha256: field here carries x-opensip-digest naming its representation, retention and authority. There is no default and no residue: a new field added without an annotation is inadmissible, exactly as in identity-schemas.v2.

Every identity text form is either the existing host form (ProjectId PROJECT-ID-V1, RequestId, ExecutionId EXECUTION-ID-V1 from c2-plan-stage-schema.v4) or a product major-two successor named in foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json (snapshot2, plan2, closure2, import2, fact2, coverage2, view2, exec-plan2, finding-key2, evidence2, run2). Workflow-owned identities are H(domain, descriptor) under the foundation canonical recipe with the domains listed in the contract; this unit never defines a second canonicalizer. No float-typed field exists anywhere in this unit; loaders refuse float lexemes, -0, duplicate keys and lone surrogates before schema validation.

EXECUTION-ID-V1: exact selector docs/coop/artifacts/c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json $.planIntent.wireTypes.executionId (grammar only; that artifact records under ownershipHonesty/RES-C2V4-01 that no producing recipe is declared anywhere in the corpus). Production values are host-minted 128-bit operational identifiers of the same shape as REQUEST-ID-V1; they are never derived from content. The reference model's values are SYNTHETIC fixture labels (see workflows_model.synthetic_execution_id) and are not a recipe. The historical R-1 fixture grammar 'execution:<text>' is not admitted by this unit.

Strict sealed logical path: relative, slash-separated, no empty/dot/dot-dot/NUL/backslash segments, each segment at most 255 bytes-as-characters. Used for snapshot inventories, edits, archive members, cwd and every identity-bearing path. Never a user-typed OS path.

A user-named OS path (baseline file, import artifact, output file). Opened only through the security unit's nofollow/ACL custody; never enters any content identity; recorded in operational records only.
Closed glob over LogicalPath: literal characters plus '*', '?' and a whole-segment '**'. No brace, class or escape syntax.

Which operational fault applies. `host-invariant` is the successor member and its scope is narrow: the closed D9ErrorCode vocabulary already published SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE with no cause mapping to it, so the host-INVARIANT subtype specifically had no representable operational-failed termination, because that class requires BOTH an errorCode and a non-none faultCause. Other host-fault causes - host-io, ledger-corrupt, provider-protocol and the rest - already existed and were always representable. PRECISION: codeMaps.rule's `total and injective` is a property of the DECLARED CAUSE DOMAIN, so an errorCode without a preimage was never a violation of totality, and this member does not `make the maps total`. It adds no error code, class, exit code or reason code, but it IS a vocabulary extension: faultCause grows by one. The inherited docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json is HISTORICAL and unchanged, so its own enum still omits the member; the selected composition is native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-public-route-registry/hostInvariantSuccessor and publishing the successor D9 artifact belongs to that unit. Borrowing host-io for a host invariant violation is refused by contract: an I/O failure and an invariant violation are different remedies.

The HOST TERMINATION deficiency vocabulary of the D9 exit contract, carried by a whole Run, analysis result or comparison step: AnalysisResult.deficiency / .secondaryDeficiencies, ComparisonStepResult.d9Deficiency and comparison-result. It is NOT the per-requirement native sufficiency vocabulary, and the two are deliberately different sets. Three members (convergence-exhausted, baseline-recipe-unsupported, query-completeness-unmet) belong to evaluation, baseline and query outcomes that no per-requirement sufficiency evaluation can produce; `none` is the whole-Run `nothing was deficient` state, which a per-requirement record expresses by satisfied=true and the absence of the field. Four native sufficiency outcomes (derivation-policy-unmet, external-consumers-unknown, input-closure-incomplete, resolution-incomplete) have NO member here at all: they project outward as their own DomainDetailCode members and as the D9 class `indeterminate` (3) with the existing error code, per native-evidence.md section 10. Widening this enum to carry them was refused: it would put per-requirement causes into a whole-Run vocabulary and would change the D9 exit contract. Use #/$defs/NativeSufficiencyDeficiency wherever the value is one requirement's own outcome. PROVENANCE: this ENUM is unchanged from the inherited D9 exit contract and no member was added, removed or reordered by any correction in this series. The DEFINITION BYTES of this $defs entry did change, because this description was added; an earlier handoff said the definition was byte-unchanged, which was true only of the enum.

The IMPORTED-EVIDENCE per-requirement outcome vocabulary, owned by imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law. It applies to a repair EvidenceRequirement whose relation is `runtime-observation` or `history-change` - relations that mint no fact2, carry no sourceUniverse/targetUniverse and have no Coverage entry, so native section 4.6 `sufficiency_v2` cannot produce an outcome for them and is not asked to. Every member is bound to the payload field that grounds it, and EACH KIND REPORTS ONLY ITS OWN: a runtime requirement is projected through observability, observationWindow and observedPopulation; a history requirement through revisionRange and collectionScope, which are its BOUNDS fields - HistoryPayloadV1 has others, notably its subjects, but it carries no observationWindow, observedPopulation or observability at all. A satisfied imported requirement means the condition was met over the BOUND window or range - not that the evidence is positive: `observed-hit` is positive execution evidence and `observable-unhit` is bounded NEGATIVE evidence, and the disclosure records which satisfied it. No imported observation establishes a universal negative, and imported evidence can never BY ITSELF establish the native closed world or authorize an unsafe delete or replace - though it may be an additional required condition alongside an already-established native basis.

GENERATED/DRIFT-CHECKED from the law's outcome keys in its declared precedence order. It is a DIFFERENT vocabulary from NativeSufficiencyDeficiency and the two never mix: a native requirement carrying an imported outcome, or the reverse, is refused.

The NATIVE PER-REQUIREMENT sufficiency outcome vocabulary: the exact nine members of DeficiencyV2, whose only defined producer is native-evidence.md section 4.6 `sufficiency_v2`, evaluated once per requirement. A record carrying one requirement's own outcome carries THIS vocabulary and never D9Deficiency, because four of these nine members have no D9Deficiency preimage and the D9-mapped value for all four is the same `verdict-indeterminate`, which would collapse exactly the distinction native-evidence.md section 10 preserves per row - including `resolution-incomplete`, the outcome section 4.6 step 6 mandates for a universal negative under unresolvedEdgePolicy=forbid over an affected target, and the outcome a destructive unused-code repair recipe turns on. This record-level vocabulary is orthogonal to two other things and replaces neither: the PUBLIC D9 TERMINATION of the Run that carries the requirement (still #/$defs/D9Deficiency and the section 10 class/code columns), and the retained CAUSE CARRIER of the Coverage entry the outcome was read from (still entry.nativeCause or the named structured carrier, per the native deficiency-cause registry). `none` is deliberately absent: a satisfied requirement is satisfied=true with the field omitted, which is what sufficiency_v2 returns.
native/native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry/perRequirementConsumerBoundary

GENERATED/DRIFT-CHECKED: this enum is exactly DeficiencyV2 in DeficiencyV2's own declared member order, mirrored here because the workflows schema bundle resolves only urn:opensip:product-v1:workflows:* references and takes no cross-bundle $ref. It is the same closed vocabulary, not a workflows-owned successor: a member added or removed on either side is a drift failure, never a widening of this one.
Generated/drift-checked from docs/coop/design-corrections/public-detail-registry.v1.json. Every owner joins the same closed registry; unknown names refuse. These details do not create D9 codes.

This typed record declares exactly one condition - a capability the selected product requires that this release did not declare available - so its code is that condition, not any DomainDetailCode. An earlier revision referenced the whole enum and admitted CONFIG.INVALID on a release-absence notice.

One capability the selected product requires that this release did not declare available, for ONE requested unit. The ownership tuple is carried in TYPED FIELDS - capabilityId, languageMode and the unit's own workspaceRoot - and is never concatenated into `subject`: workspaceRoot is a UserInputPath bounded at 4096 while BoundedText is 1024, so a concatenated subject could silently truncate a path and collapse two distinct requested units into one indistinguishable notice. Advisory: it terminates nothing, mints no Coverage, grants no Control verdict or repair authority, and is never a clone Candidate.

The invocation's availability account, composed PER STEP. An earlier revision used one flat array bounded at 1024 and argued it could not truncate because that is the analysis-spec bound - but 1024 is per analysis-spec, not per invocation, and a named multi-step invocation carries up to 64 steps: two admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046 notices and the flat array refused. Composing per step preserves every valid admitted invocation: each step keeps its own bounded collection, `steps` is bounded by the invocation step bound (StepId 0..63), and no notice is ever discarded to fit. `totalNoticeCount` is the sum of the step counts and is authoritative for a caller counting absences across the invocation. A step that made no selection - a skipped step, or a non-analysis step - contributes NO entry; a step that selected and found nothing absent contributes an entry with an empty array, which is the positive statement that it checked. A retried step keeps ONE entry, for the attempt whose selection the invocation retained.

D9-shaped per-step or aggregate termination. exitCode is never stored; it derives from class by the fixed table (0,1,2,3,4,130). Branch contract: success carries no errorCode/reasonCodes/signal; policy-failed requires runId, or authority=ephemeral when the failing analysis was explicitly non-authoritative and therefore has no Run; request-rejected and operational-failed require errorCode (operational-failed also a non-none faultCause); indeterminate requires reasonCodes; interrupted requires signal and may carry runId only when a Run was committed before the interrupt.

Mandatory correspondence of external evidence to analyzed source. exact-snapshot binds a snapshot2 and is the only correspondence that is mapped by itself. vcs-revision binds a commit plus dirty flag and optional build identity; a commit string (even clean) or a declared build identity is a STATEMENT and cannot prove which generated/runtime bytes correspond to which snapshot bytes, so vcs-revision evidence is consumable only when an admitted SourceMappingV1 (imported-evidence schema) joins every consumed generated path to a snapshot2 inventory entry by digest; otherwise it is unmapped-only. The wrapper's sourceCorrespondenceDigest is the raw SHA-256 of this record's canonical bytes, retained as a blob.
raw SHA-256 of the canonical SourceMappingV1 bytes admitted with this evidence, or null when none was supplied (then vcs-revision evidence is unmapped-only)
Exact product H(security.repair-apply-authorization.v1, admitted RepairApplyAuthorizationV1) with the security.repair-apply-authorization.v1 prefix; current host admission is mandatory.

Complete current pin inventory observed under the purge writer lease. Operational pinId is a host-ledger name scoped to this Run, not a content identity or authority token. Never truncate this disclosure or infer destructive consent from it.

The availability account of ONE analysis step's own selection, associated with that step by stepId. `notices` is bounded at 1024 because that is the analysis-spec requestedCapabilities bound and one selection produces at most one absence per requested row, so a STEP's collection can never truncate and its noticeCount always equals its array length. The same ownership tuple may recur in different steps - two steps may select the same unit - so uniqueness is within a step, never across the invocation.

Import is an operational admission step (import custody), never an analysis Run. There is exactly ONE import identity: importId = H('import', foundation import descriptor) from foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/import (schemaVersion 2). The typed payload records here (runtime, test, history) and native's typed records (dependency-source, prepared-output, and native's runtime-coverage/test-results/history payload grammars) are PAYLOADS: their bytes are referenced by payloadDigest (raw SHA-256 of the canonical payload bytes) and their registered schema by payloadSchemaDigest. The wrapper's identity therefore differs from the payload content hash, and one payload can appear under two wrappers only if correspondence/producer/adapter/scope also agree, which is the intended meaning. Hostile-input bounds: artifact at most 268435456 bytes; at most 1048576 subjects; at most 4096 blobs; JSON depth at most 32; strict UTF-8, no duplicate keys, no float lexemes, no surrogates. Observed no-hits during one window are never universal non-use; only observable-unhit subjects may be consumed by a predicate, and only with the window/population disclosed.

Normative and closed. A policy atom may name a relation from exactly two places: the thirteen NATIVE fact relations closed by foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-relation-registry, or the imported-evidence relations below. An atom naming anything else refuses at policy admission; there is no open relation namespace and no default.

Atoms range over imported-evidence subjects as well as native facts, and the same per-relation ladder law must decide their minResolution. Without a ladder for these relations the atom's rung is undecidable, which is the other half of the withdrawn abstract-tier vocabulary. These relations are deliberately NOT added to the native fact registry: they mint no fact2, they carry no sourceUniverse/targetUniverse, and that registry stays closed at thirteen.
Closed table row: which registered payload schema each import kind admits and which contract owns the payload semantics.

ONE registry, five rows: runtime/test/history admit ONLY the workflow payload domains (native's runtime-coverage/test-results/history adapter grammars are normalized by native into these payloads BEFORE import and are not import payload domains); dependency/prepared admit ONLY native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1 / native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1 (native-evidence.md §7 spellings).
the registered schema DOCUMENT whose exact complete bytes hash to payloadSchemaDigest (raw SHA-256 of the file bytes; no canonical-schema hash exists)
JSON pointer of the payload $def inside schemaDocument; the selector identifies the definition, the digest binds the document bytes

The one closed import payload registry. Exactly these five rows exist; any other (kind, payloadDomain) pair is IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH and a domain with no row is IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED.

The one closed mapping artifact that makes vcs-revision/declared-build evidence consumable. Producing recipe: the adapter that generated the runtime/test artifact emits, for every generated path it observed, the digest of the generated bytes and the digest and path of the snapshot source it was built from; the host admits the mapping only when every sourceSha256 equals the snapshot2 inventory digest of sourcePath (else IMPORT.SOURCE_MAPPING_REQUIRED and the evidence stays unmapped-only). Digest: raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes, retained as a blob and carried in SourceCorrespondence.sourceMappingDigest.
sorted ascending by generatedPath; generatedPath unique

Exact mirror of foundation identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/scope-descriptor: the foundation record is the AUTHORITY and this document restates it field-for-field, including every array's owning x-opensip-order. wrapper.scopeDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of this record (the same producing rule as plan.scopeDigest); retained as a blob. There is no separate workflow import-scope domain. Because one digest preimage is admitted through both documents, they must admit and refuse exactly the same bytes; the mirror-drift check proves it rather than asserting it.
Closed preimage of wrapper.observationDigest (raw SHA-256 of canonical bytes; retained blob). Null members mean the observation semantics do not apply to the kind.
Closed preimage of wrapper.buildDigest (raw SHA-256 of canonical bytes; retained blob).

Exact mirror of foundation import descriptor fields (schemaVersion 2). Every auxiliary digest is a raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of an exact closed record retained as a blob (identity-and-evidence §2 auxiliary-digest rule); none is an H(domain) identity: payloadSchemaDigest = raw SHA-256 of the exact registered schema DOCUMENT bytes (PayloadRegistryV1 row); payloadDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical payload bytes; sourceCorrespondenceDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical common#SourceCorrespondence; buildDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical BuildIdentityV1; scopeDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical ImportScopeDescriptor (= foundation scope-descriptor); observationDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical ImportObservationV1. importId = 'import2:' + H('import', this object) is the only H-domain identity in an import. No hidden metadata: every field is one of these thirteen.
Operational custody record joining the wrapper, its payload binding, the resolved correspondence and staleness for a given Plan. Only importId enters the Plan (plan.importIds).
unobservable: the capture could not observe this subject (no source map, not instrumented); unmapped: no correspondence to an inventoried source path. Neither is ever an unhit signal.
Payload domain workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1. Its raw canonical bytes hash to wrapper.payloadDigest.
sorted strictly ascending by (path, symbol) UTF-8 bytes
Payload domain workflow.import-payload.history.v1. Advisory priority input only.
Closed decision table row for staleness classification relative to a Plan's snapshot binding.

commit-equal-clean-mapped: commit equal, clean, and an admitted SourceMappingV1 joins every generated path to the Plan snapshot by digest → current/consumable. commit-equal-clean-unmapped: commit and clean flag alone → current/unmapped-only (a commit string cannot prove byte correspondence).

Normative and CLOSED. THE outcome law for a repair EvidenceRequirement whose relation is one of the two imported-evidence relations registered above. It adds no relation, no rung, no import kind, no payload domain and no D9 class, code or exit.

Each relation may report only the outcomes its own payload can ground. A history requirement can never report a runtime observability or window outcome, and a runtime requirement can never report a history range or collection-scope outcome; the producer refuses rather than borrowing the other kind's projection.

EvidenceRequirement carries only relation, minResolution, completeness, satisfied and deficiency. Every other input this law reads is named here with the field that owns it, so no untyped caller value stands in for a measured Run.

Normative and CLOSED, and a SELECTED CLARIFICATION rather than a restatement: nothing before this published how a repair target reaches an imported payload subject. It introduces no new record and no new field; it names the retained records that already carry the join.

A policy is data. Every construct is a closed object with a fixed 'op' or field set; there is no string expression language, no script, hook, include, or reference to repository code. The predicate grammar is exactly the evaluator's predicate set from the identity contract §4 (exists, none, count-at-most, all-covered, and, or, not) over typed fact-field filters, evaluated with strong Kleene three-valued logic. Bounds: at most 512 rules; at most 64 predicate nodes per rule; nesting depth at most 8; at most 16 filters per atom; at most 4096 waivers. Policy, scope and resolved waiver digests are raw SHA-256 of the canonical closed document bytes, retained as blobs; they are not H-domain identities.

A resolution rung NAME. This replaces the withdrawn abstract Resolution tier vocabulary (syntax/resolved/type/external), which was disjoint from the rung names every fact, Coverage entry and native RequirementV2 actually carries, had no published mapping onto them, and was compared by a single global rank table across all relations. The inherited C-1 law is that ordering is PER-RELATION and never global, so an abstract tier could only ever be a partial, lossy, relation-dependent renaming of the rung it names; the atom now names the rung directly. This enum is the flat vocabulary and is a NECESSARY condition only: it is exactly the union of the ladders in foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-relation-registry (the single ladder authority) and is drift-checked against it. Membership of THIS atom's relation's ladder is the sufficient condition and is enforced at admission, because no schema keyword can express it without restating the ladders and creating another independent source.
required: absent/stale/unmapped evidence makes the rule indeterminate. optional: the rule evaluates without it and discloses IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE.

Any other identifier refuses at policy admission. The identifier syntax is all a schema keyword can express here; closed membership is decided at admission against those two registries, which are the authorities.

Proposed Atom extension: optional endpoint. Root integrates into policy-document.schema.json. Default source when omitted.

Repository code execution is disabled by default. A test-execution step is admitted only when selected explicitly, the security unit admits a RepoExecutionGrantV2 with principal P-TRUSTED-REPO and executionClass test-runner bound to this projectId, snapshot digest and the exact argv digest (expiry operation-end, never inherited), and CI mode uses a pre-existing policy record rather than interactive consent. The host spawns the exact argv with no shell: argv[0] is either a LogicalPath member of the sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain closure2; the environment is constructed from the allowlist only; cwd is a LogicalPath inside the project root. The host DISCLOSES network and process reach (copied from the security unit's platform truth table); it does not confine them and refuses any step that claims it does. The outcome is evidence (an import2 wrapper with kind=test), never Coverage and never a verdict.

clauses.text:
**Standing:** Authored and corrected by actual Claude, Codex and actual Grok
under D-367 delegated design authority for the D-371 intended product. Review
and application standing is governed by the [correction record](../../../coop/design-corrections/README.md)
and central readiness register. Historical reviews apply only to their frozen
bytes; this consolidated successor requires its own independent review and
application. Reference results do not establish platform qualification. Reference checks in
[`docs/coop/design-corrections/native/`](../../../coop/design-corrections/native/README.md)
are design evidence, not product measurement. This revision answers the twelve
items retained in `reviews/native-author-feedback.v1.md` (F1–F12) and seven
further CHANGES_REQUIRED items, R1–R7 (co-located per-language units, inert
generated-file inputs, single canonical import payloads, closed joins H-1…H-5,
import-only clone exclusion, Config2/backup custody join, fault law). The only
retained record of R1–R7 is their statement in
`native/native-cases.v2.json#feedbackMap` and the README table; no separate
Codex review document for them is retained in the repository, and none is
claimed. The post-reset independent Claude review of the frozen
`candidate-subject.v1` (retained in the repository at
`docs/coop/design-corrections/reviews/post-reset-review.v1/review.md` with
executable probes) returned MUST-3, SHOULD-4 and SHOULD-7 against this unit; the
new author session's corrections and handoff are retained at
`docs/coop/design-corrections/reviews/post-reset-author.v1/handoff.md` (items
`PR-MUST-3`, `PR-SHOULD-4` in the feedback map). The second independent review,
of the frozen `candidate-subject.v2`, returned N-1 (nested repository/project
boundaries not carried into unit discovery or the Plan scope) and advisory A-3
(an explicit Cargo workspace root lost member folding) against this unit; a
further Claude author session corrected them here (items `PR2-P3`, `PR2-P22`:
§1.4 U-2, U-8, §10, §13 H-8). The earlier author handoff file
`reviews/native-fix-handoff.v3.md` is empty (the authoring session was
interrupted), is cited nowhere as evidence and is no longer a consumed source
of the checker. A third independent session — a fresh blind consumer
reconstruction of the accepted `candidate-subject.v5` subset — returned M-1 (no producing
recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment`), M-2 (no TypeScript native-context record) and
advisories A-1/A-2 against this unit; a further Claude author session corrected them here
(§0, §2.2, §2.3, §2.4, §4.1a, §9.4, §10, §11, §12, §13; items `CB-M1`, `CB-M2`, `CB-A1`,
`CB-A2` in the feedback map) and swept §13/§14 for obligations already discharged in current
bytes. These are successor edits: the acceptance of `candidate-subject.v5` does not cover
them, and they require a fresh independent review of a newly frozen subject.

**Resolves:** AR-07 (sealed Rust dependency inputs and an honest execution
boundary), AR-12 (examination completeness is not resolution completeness),
AR-13 native cells (exact TypeScript/JavaScript/Rust cells, mixed repositories,
clone equivalence modes, zero-config recognition, import evidence payloads).
Owner rows: DR-118/119 (cells, inputs, execution limits), DR-004 (resolution
completeness law), DR-118 (import payload semantics).

**Joint interfaces honored.** Product source identity is `snapshot2`, Plan is
`plan2`, product fact records are `fact2`, coverage is `coverage2` over a
`CoverageResultV3` payload, and every import is one `import2` wrapper from
`foundation/identity-schemas.v3.json`. Unchanged native and input identities
retain those major-two recipes. Current evaluator output is identity §4 profile
3: `subject3`, `finding3`, `proof3`, `evidence3`, `seal3`, `run3` and
`policy-derivation3`. Mixed output-major graphs refuse. Historical `run2` /
`finding2` / `evidence2` / `seal2` / `proof2` bytes remain byte-specific; they
are never relabelled as current. This contract authors typed payloa…

The retained selector's own deferral, `"SHAPE ONLY; computation and verification stay deferred (R1-C2-03)"`, and its `EXAMPLE ENCODING for the fixtures only` note are historical bytes that stay unchanged and remain a non-recipe; §4.1a supplies the successor producing recipe the …

A cell is `capability × languageMode × platformFamily`. The machine-readable
matrix is `native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json`, validated by
`NativeCapabilityMatrixV2`; its `cells` array is the **complete product** of its
own `capabilities` and `languageModes`, and the reference checks hold it to
exactly that product rather than to a number written here. (A literal count in
this prose said `60` while the matrix held 66; a second hand-maintained counter
would only go stale again, so the count is derived from the two arrays and
reported by the checks instead of restated.) Platform families are exactly the
four `platformId`
values in the delivery release inventory: `linux-x86_64-gnu`,
`linux-aarch64-gnu`, `macos-aarch64`, `macos-x86_64`. The OS/kernel/libc/filesystem
*baseline* that qualifies a machine into a family is owned by the security unit
(AR-06); this contract states only that native capabilities are platform-invariant
by design (`platformInvariantDesign: true`) and that no cell is `QUALIFIED` here.

Cell states (closed): `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` (contracted behavior, corpus named,
qualification pending), `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` (refuses with the named deficiency;
never silently narrows), `NOT-SELECTED` (outside D-371; no promise).

| Mode id | Recognition | Universe | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts-tsconfig` | `tsconfig.json` at the unit root (or named by discovery), `allowJs` absent/false | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=tsconfig` | JavaScript files are not program roots; a JS import target is `unresolved-module-specifier`. |
| `js-allowjs` | `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` with effective `allowJs=true` (jsconfig defaults `allowJs=true`) | `typescript-v2`, `allowJs=true` | `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` are program roots. |
| `js-synthesized` | Inside a `tsjs` unit already discovered by §1.4 U-1: no `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` at the unit root, so the `package.json` marker selects this mode. `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` files under that unit are program roots; they do not themselves make a unit | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=synthesized`, `synthesizerVersion=1` | Host synthesizes `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` (§2.2); Plan-bound with `DEFAULTED` provenance, disclosed in output. |
| `rust-cargo` | `Cargo.toml` at the unit root (package or workspace) | `rust-v2` | Requires a sealed `DependencySourceSetV1` when the lock lists any non-path package (§3). |
| `rust-cargo-prepared` | as above, plus an admitted `PreparedOutputSetV3` of inert rows | `rust-v2` with `preparedOutputSetId` non-null | Expansions and directives are consumed as data; a site without a row is an unresolved edge (§3.6). |
| `syntax-only` | any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar | `syntax-v2` (grammar-only; no compiler) | Inventory/syntax/clones only; semantic rungs `language-tier-unsupported`. |

**This table selects a MODE; it does not discover units.** No Recognition cell
mints a unit. For the five rows that name a **compilation** universe —
`ts-tsconfig`, `js-allowjs`, `js-synthesized`, `rust-cargo` and
`rust-cargo-prepared` — the cell is read **after** §1.4 U-1 has yielded a unit of
that language family, because those modes describe a program and a program needs
one. **`syntax-only` carries no such prerequisite and must not be read as if it
did:** it is the compiler-free path, it has no compilation unit at all (§1.2's

The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
share a root.

**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.

`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.

- **U-1 (one unit per directory and language family)** A directory holding
  `Cargo.toml` yields a `rust` unit; a directory holding `tsconfig.json`,
  `jsconfig.json` or `package.json` yields exactly one `tsjs` unit whose mode is
  chosen by precedence `tsconfig.json` (→ `ts-tsconfig`/`js-allowjs`) >
  `jsconfig.json` (→ `js-allowjs`) > `package.json` (→ `js-synthesized`). The
  precedence selects the mode **within** `tsjs`; it never removes the co-located
  `rust` unit. A root with both markers has two units with the same `rootPath`
  (`units-colocated-cargo-and-package-json-root-keeps-both-languages`).
- **U-2 (Cargo workspace folding)** A `Cargo.toml` package inside a Cargo
  workspace root's tree is folded into the workspace unit as a member package
  (Cargo resolves the workspace as one program); it is listed in
  `memberPackageRoots`, not as a separate unit. A standalone package outside any
  workspace is its own `cargo-package` unit. **Explicit roots are unit
  selection, never loss of Cargo workspace semantics (post-reset v2 A-3/P22):**
  naming a Cargo workspace root explicitly yields exactly the automatic result
  for that unit (members folded, member `target` output pruned, a member's
  `src/target` still source); naming a member package alone selects that package
  as its own `cargo-package` unit, and files of the unselected root or siblings
  are honest `no-program-unit-for-language` rows, neither claimed nor
  over-ignored (`units-explicit-cargo-workspace-root-keeps-member-folding-and-member-target-pruning`).
- **U-3 (deterministic membership within a language)** A file's family is fixed
  by extension (`.rs` → `rust`; `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` → `tsjs`).
  It belongs to the **deepest unit of its own family** whose root prefixes its
  path. Units of another family never claim it. Nested monorepo packages
  (`packages/web/tsconfig.json` under a root `tsconfig.json`) are therefore
  distinct `tsjs` units and the deeper one wins for its subtree
  (`units-nested-monorepo-deepest-within-language-and-workspace-folding`).
- **U-4 (no source erasure; honest unsupported files)** Every snapshot inventory
  file appears in exactly one `FileMembershipRowV1`: `program-member`;
  `syntax-only` with reason `no-program-unit-for-language` (a `.rs` file with no
  enclosing Rust unit: semantic rungs `unknown`, cause `no-program-unit`),
  `grammar-only` (bundled grammar, no program) or `host-ignore-convention`
  (the file lies inside a pruned tree of the shared rule below); or
  `unsupported-file` with reason `no-bundled-grammar`, listed in
  `unsupportedFiles`. `erasedFiles` is a schema-constant empty array
  (`maxItems 0`) and the model refuses a membership that does not cover the
  inventory exactly once.
- **U-4a (one shared discovery rule; post-reset MUST-3)** The host ignore
  conventions and unit enumeration are stated once, in
  `docs/coop/design-corrections/discovery-defaults.py`, and consumed by both
  `discover_units`/`assign_membership`/`unit_scope_descriptor`/`typescript_mode`
  …
